approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Medicare Levy and Medicare Levy Surcharge) Bill 2018
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would raise the income cut-offs below which certain people do not pay the Medicare levy or the Medicare levy surcharge.
It would update these thresholds in line with consumer price index movements for the 2017-18 income year.
The government says this would keep the same people exempt as in the previous year if their incomes rose no more than inflation.
The Medicare levy low-income thresholds for individuals, families and the dependent child-student component would increase.
The Medicare levy low-income thresholds for those eligible for the seniors and pensioners tax offset would also increase.
The Medicare levy surcharge low-income threshold would increase as well.
Low-income individuals, families, seniors and pensioners.

Labor supported the bill indexing Medicare levy thresholds to CPI, raising individual thresholds to $21,980 and family thresholds to $37,089. The speaker also argued for splitting the government's tax bill to give immediate relief to low- and middle-income earners, noting Labor's proposal would give $400 more to those earning under $125,000, and cited Grattan Institute analysis showing the government's later-stage tax cuts would make the system more regressive.

The speaker argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (Medicare Levy and Medicare Levy Surcharge) Bill 2018 adjusts low-income thresholds in line with CPI to prevent low-income families from paying the Medicare levy, and highlighted record government investment in Medicare, hospitals, schools, disability services, and the PBS, including $34.4 billion added to the Medicare Guarantee Fund and $35.3 billion for MBS and PBS expenditure in 2018-19.

The government argued that a stronger economy allowed it to scrap a planned Medicare levy increase and instead raise the Medicare levy low-income threshold, exempting more low-income earners from the levy in 2017-18. Specific new thresholds include $21,980 for individuals and $34,758 for single senior pensioners.
Treasury Laws Amendment (Medicare Levy and Medicare Levy Surcharge) Act 2018
